:::{#thm-held-out-unbiased}
#### Held-out mean squared error estimates the generalization error

Let a [prediction rule](#def-prediction-rule) $\fitted$
be fitted to a [training set](#def-training-set) $\trainset$,
and let a [held-out set](#def-held-out-set) of $m$ observations
$(X_{0,1}, Y_{0,1}), \ldots, (X_{0,m}, Y_{0,m})$
be drawn from the same population as $(X_0, Y_0)$,
each independently of $\trainset$.
Then, given $\trainset$,
the expected [mean squared error](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-mse)
of the held-out predictions
is the [generalization error](#def-generalization-error):

$$
\E{\frac{1}{m} \sum_{j=1}^m \sqf{\fitted(X_{0,j}) - Y_{0,j}} \mid \trainset}
= \generr_{\trainset}.
$$

:::

::: proof
This is @sol-held-out-unbiased.
:::
